facts.heading: Anxiety worsened in September
facts.content: Hannah has been anxious all the time, and it got worse in September.
facts.evidence: I'm just anxious all the time and it got worse in September.

facts.heading: Became deputy head
facts.content: Hannah was the deputy head at her school.
facts.evidence: I was my deputy head at my school.

facts.heading: Taught for eleven years
facts.content: Hannah has taught at her school for 11 years.
facts.evidence: I've taught here for 11 years and I love it.

facts.heading: Struggles with job recognition
facts.content: Hannah keeps thinking people picked the wrong person for the deputy role.
facts.evidence: I keep thinking they picked the wrong person and that sooner or later someone will notice

facts.heading: Rehearses meeting scenarios
facts.content: Hannah rehearses what she would say for possible questions in meetings.
facts.evidence: I start rehearsing Monday's stuff meeting in my head

facts.heading: Worries about being judged
facts.content: Hannah imagines people thinking she is out of her depth.
facts.evidence: What do you imagine they would think? That I'm out of my depth

facts.heading: Rewrote email four times
facts.content: Hannah rewrote an email to the governors four times.
facts.evidence: Last week I rewrote the same email to the governors four times.

facts.heading: Fear of seeming stupid
facts.content: Hannah was afraid Mr Hargraves would think she was stupid.
facts.evidence: I was afraid Mr Hargraves, the chair of governors, would think that I was stupid.

facts.heading: Mr Hargraves was kind
facts.content: Mr Hargraves has been kind to Hannah.
facts.evidence: He has been nothing but kind. He told me in September he was delighted.

facts.heading: Feels like she is lying
facts.content: Hannah feels like she is lying to Mr Hargraves about her capabilities.
facts.evidence: It makes it worse somehow, because I feel like I'm lying to him.

facts.heading: Feels like a child
facts.content: Hannah feels like a child wearing her mother's coat most days.
facts.evidence: Most days I feel like a child wearing her mother's coat.

facts.heading: Mother was a head teacher
facts.content: Hannah's mother was a head teacher for 20 years.
facts.evidence: She was a head teacher for 20 years.

facts.heading: Mother was brilliant
facts.content: Hannah's mother was brilliant, and people still compliment her.
facts.evidence: She was brilliant. Everyone in the village still stops me saying what a wonderful hat she was.

facts.heading: Compares self to mother
facts.content: Hannah compares everything she does to what her mother would have done better.
facts.evidence: Everything I do, I think, would she have done it better?

facts.heading: Mother's support is surface
facts.content: Hannah's mother is supportive on the surface.
facts.evidence: She is very supportive on the surface.

facts.heading: Feels like making a fuss
facts.content: Hannah feels like she is making a fuss to avoid telling her mother the extent of her feelings.
facts.evidence: It makes me feel like I'm making a fuss so I don't tell her how bad it is.

facts.heading: Waking at four every morning
facts.content: Hannah is awake at four every morning and goes through a to-do list.
facts.evidence: That I'm awake at four every morning. I fall asleep fine. Then I'm awake at four going through the to-do list.

facts.heading: Waking since term started
facts.content: Hannah has been waking up this way since the second week of term.
facts.evidence: Since about the second week of term, I drink a lot of coffee to get through the day, which I know doesn't help.

facts.heading: High coffee consumption
facts.content: Hannah drinks five or six cups of coffee daily.
facts.evidence: Five or six.

facts.heading: Physical symptoms in afternoons
facts.content: Hannah experiences a fast heart rate and shaky hands in the afternoons.
facts.evidence: My heart goes fast. My hands are a bit shaky.

facts.heading: Exhaustion from pretending
facts.content: Hannah feels exhausted by the end of every day from pretending.
facts.evidence: I am exhausted by the end of every day, just from pretending.

facts.heading: Partner Ben's advice
facts.content: Ben suggested Hannah should just enjoy her situation.
facts.evidence: He says I should just enjoy it.

facts.heading: Feeling guilty and alone
facts.content: Hannah feels guilty and a bit alone when Ben gives advice.
facts.evidence: Guilty and a bit alone.

facts.heading: Lost friends at school
facts.content: Hannah no longer has friends at school who have talked to her.
facts.evidence: Not anymore, not really. I used to eat lunch in the year 4 corridor with the others.

facts.heading: Lost company with promotion
facts.content: Hannah lost some company along with her promotion.
facts.evidence: So you lost some company along with the promotion? Yes, I hadn't thought of it like that.

facts.heading: Missed classes and promotion
facts.content: Hannah missed her classes and accepted the promotion because she couldn't say no.
facts.evidence: I missed my class too. I thought I did. I said yes in the room because I couldn't say no to her.

facts.heading: Tears about fear
facts.content: Hannah cried after accepting the promotion due to fear and fear of not going back.
facts.evidence: Fear, I think. And that I would never get to go back.

facts.heading: Last time feeling relaxed
facts.content: Hannah felt properly relaxed during the summer holidays.
facts.evidence: These summer holidays, we went walking in the lakes and I didn't think about school once for ten days.

facts.heading: Relaxation during holiday
facts.content: During the holiday, nobody expected anything of Hannah.
facts.evidence: Nobody expected anything of me. I was just walking.

facts.heading: Relapse before term started
facts.content: The week before a term started, Hannah was a wreck again.
facts.evidence: The week before a term, I was a wreck again. I couldn't eat on the Sunday.

facts.heading: Tried writing down good things
facts.content: Hannah started writing down what went well each evening. This helped for about two weeks.
facts.evidence: I started writing down what went well each evening. Small things. A cheer of laughing. A good email. It helped for about two weeks and then I stopped because I felt silly.

facts.heading: Felt silly about bragging
facts.content: Hannah felt silly when writing down good things. She felt like she was bragging to herself.
facts.evidence: As if I were bragging to myself in a notebook. Noticing what went well was not the same as bragging. It just felt that way.

facts.heading: Wants to do job without fraud
facts.content: Hannah would like to do her job without feeling like a fraud. This involves not rehearsing meetings or sending emails repeatedly.
facts.evidence: I would like to do the job without feeling like a fraud. Mmm, walking into a meeting and not rehearsing it first, sending an email once.

facts.heading: Wants calm evenings
facts.content: Hannah wants to be able to sit on the sofa in the evening without stomach knots.
facts.evidence: Being able to sit on the sofa in the evening without my stomach in knots.

facts.heading: Feelings about goals
facts.content: Hannah felt light and a bit tearful when stating her goals out loud.
facts.evidence: Lightful. Lighter. A bit tearful, actually.

facts.heading: First time sharing bad news
facts.content: Hannah stated that this was the first time she had told anyone how bad something is.
facts.evidence: That's the first time I've told anyone how bad it is.

facts.heading: Fear of telling Ben
facts.content: Hannah feels scared about telling Ben about the 4AM issue. She fears he would hear she didn't say sooner.
facts.evidence: Scary. He would probably be heard that I didn't say sooner.

facts.heading: Choosing quiet time to share
facts.content: Hannah might try telling someone this week if she chooses a quiet moment.
facts.evidence: I might try this week.

facts.heading: Preferred time to share
facts.content: Hannah prefers to share when she chooses a quiet moment, not on a Sunday evening.
facts.evidence: If I choose a quiet moment, not on a Sunday evening, then I'm too warmed up.

facts.heading: Preferred time for sharing
facts.content: Hannah suggested Saturday morning over breakfast as a time to share.
facts.evidence: Saturday morning, perhaps? Yeah, over breakfast. He is always in a good mood then.

facts.heading: Will try evening notebook again
facts.content: Hannah agreed to try the evening notebook again for one week, even just one line.
facts.evidence: I could. I will put it by the kettle so I don't forget.

facts.heading: Nearly cancelled session
facts.content: Hannah nearly cancelled the session this morning. She was glad she did not cancel.
facts.evidence: Only did I nearly cancel this morning. I'm glad I didn't.
